'''''Vitis californica''''', with [[common name]]s '''California wild grape''', '''Northern California grape''', and '''Pacific grape''',<ref>{{GRIN | access-date=7 July 2015}}</ref> is a wild [[grape]] species native to western North America.

==Description==
''Vitis californica'' is a [[deciduous]] vine. It is fast growing and can grow to over {{convert|10|m}} in length.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=California Grape, Vitis californica |url=https://calscape.org/Vitis-californica-(California-Grape) |access-date=2022-10-01 |website=Calscape, California Native Plant Society}}</ref> It climbs on other plants or covers the ground with twisted, woody ropes of vine covered in green leaves. It typically flowers in May and June. In autumn, the leaves turn orange and yellow before falling.<ref name=":1" />

[[Image:Vitis californica at Caswell Memorial State Park spring leaves.jpg|thumb|New leaves in a [[riparian]] woodland in the [[San Joaquin Valley]]]]
==Distribution and habitat==

The species is widespread across much of [[California]] as well as southwestern [[Oregon]].<ref name=jepson>Jepson Flora: [http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_JM_treatment.pl?Vitis+californica ''Vitis californica'']</ref><ref>[http://bonap.net/MapGallery/County/Vitis%20californica.png Biota of North America Program 2014 county distribution map]</ref><ref name=":1">[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-calrecnum=8321 Calflora taxon report, ''Vitis californica''  Benth. California grape,  California wild grape ]</ref> It is distributed along the [[Coast Ranges]] from [[Douglas County, Oregon]], south to [[San Luis Obispo County]], California; in the [[Klamath Mountains]], the [[Cascade Range]], and the [[Sierra Nevada]] from Siskiyou to Kern counties, California; and in the [[Central Valley (California)|Central Valley]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Howard |first=Janet L. |date=1993 |title=Vitis californica In: Fire Effects Information System |url=https://www.fs.usda.gov/database/feis/plants/vine/vitcal/all.html |access-date=2022-10-01 |website=U.S. Department of Agriculture, Forest Service}}</ref>
The grapes are a common sight along the banks of the [[Sacramento River]].

The plant grows in canyons, alongside springs, and streams. It tends to thrive in damp conditions and so it is common in riparian areas.<ref name=":0" /> It can be found on slopes as well as flat ground in wetland and forested habitats. Once matured<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Smither-Kopperl |first=Margaret |date=June 2022 |title=Plant Guide for California wild grape ''(Vitis californica'') |url=https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/Internet/FSE_PLANTMATERIALS/publications/capmcpg13920.pdf |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220803032908/https://www.nrcs.usda.gov/Internet/FSE_PLANTMATERIALS/publications/capmcpg13920.pdf |url-status=dead |archive-date=August 3, 2022 |access-date=2022-10-01 |website=USDA-[[Natural Resources Conservation Service]]}}</ref> like most other native California plants it can withstand periods of dry conditions.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plant Details - Kumeyaay Garden |url=https://www.sandiego.edu/kumeyaay-garden/plant.php?ID=16 |access-date=2022-10-18 |website=[[University of San Diego]] |language=en}}</ref>

==Cultivation==
===Viticulture===
The wild grape is strong and robust, and [[viticulture|viticulturists]] worldwide often use it as [[rootstock]] for their [[Vitis vinifera|wine grapes]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Dangl |first1=Gerald S. |last2=Mendum |first2=Mary Lou |last3=Yang |first3=Judy |last4=Walker |first4=M. Andrew |last5=Preece |first5=John E. |date=2015-11-19 |title=Hybridization of cultivated ''Vitis vinifera'' with wild ''V. californica'' and ''V. girdiana'' in California |journal=[[Ecology and Evolution]]|volume=5 |issue=23 |pages=5671–5684 |doi=10.1002/ece3.1797 |doi-access=free |issn=2045-7758 |pmc=4813103 |pmid=27069616}}</ref> It prefers heavier soils.<ref name=":2" /> In some areas where the plant is not native it has the capacity to become a [[noxious weed]]. However, its invasive nature can be kept under control and is very easy to pull out.<ref name=":2" />

[[File:Vitis californica Roger’s Red ripe grapes.jpg|thumb|Roger's Red, ripe]]
===Horticulture===
''Vitis californica'' is cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]]. The interesting shape and color of the leaves and the lush, trainable vines make this species an attractive garden plant. This vine is commonly used in [[native plant]] gardens, where once established it thrives without summer water.

The cultivar '{{visible anchor|Roger's Red}}' (named for noted horticulturist Roger Raiche) turns brilliant red in fall.<ref name="ornamentalgenetic" /> It is a hybrid with a wine grape, × ''Vitis vinifera'' cv. [[Alicante Bouschet]].<ref name="ornamentalgenetic">
{{cite book|year=2019|publication-place=[[Cham, Switzerland]]|publisher=[[Springer International Publishing]]|first3=Chittaranjan|first2=Andrew|first1=Dario|last3=Kole|last2=Walker|last1=Cantu|id=978-3-030-18600-5. 978-3-030-18603-6. 978-3-030-18601-2|series=[[Compendium of Plant Genomes]]|issn=2199-4781|s2cid=207988507|url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/978-3-030-18601-2|title=The Grape Genome|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-18601-2 |isbn=978-3-030-18600-5 }}{{ RP |27,34}}

This book cites this research.

{{cite journal|year=2010|issue=2|volume=61|first5=Deborah|first4=Judy|first3=Sue|first2=Roger|first1=Gerald|last5=Golino|last4=Yang|last3=Sim|last2=Raiche|last1=Dangl|pages=266–271|title=Genetic Composition of the Ornamental Grape Roger's Red|publisher=[[American Society for Enology and Viticulture]]|journal=[[American Journal of Enology and Viticulture]]|doi=10.5344/ajev.2010.61.2.266|issn=0002-9254|url=https://www.ajevonline.org/content/61/2/266|url-access=subscription}}
</ref> The cultivar 'Walker Ridge' turns yellow in the autumn.<ref>{{Cite web |title=''Vitis'' 'Roger's Red' |url=https://www.pacifichorticulture.org/articles/vitis-rogers-red/ |access-date=2022-10-20 |website=[[Pacific Horticulture]]|language=en}}</ref>

==Uses==
Bunches of small and often sour but edible purple grapes hang from the vines in autumn, which can be made into wine or jelly.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Elias|first1=Thomas S.|title=Edible Wild Plants: A North American Field Guide to Over 200 Natural Foods|last2=Dykeman|first2=Peter A.|publisher=[[Sterling Publishing|Sterling]]|year=2009|isbn=978-1-4027-6715-9|location=New York|pages=214, 216|oclc=244766414|orig-year=1982}}</ref> The grapes provide an important food source for a variety of wild animals, especially birds, and the foliage provides thick cover.
